sections.h2: Which selling route suits a Lubbock owner short on time?
sections.html:
A short timeline usually points to a cash buyer, while a full listing suits an owner who can wait. Lubbock sellers weigh three things: how the roof, plumbing and floors look, whether any liens sit on the title, and how soon the proceeds are needed.

Texas Tech University, a large medical center and the farm trade give the city steady demand. A house near campus or a hospital tends to draw investors and renters as well as families, so even a dated property has a market.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, though showings, repair requests and lender timelines stretch the calendar.
  • Owner sale: skips the commission and puts pricing and paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: quick close, no repairs, typically priced under a polished retail sale.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Lubbock's setting and history?
sections.html:
Lubbock sits at 3,256 feet on the flat South Plains, along Interstate 27, 327 miles northwest of Dallas. The Texas State Historical Association says two rival settlements, Old Lubbock and Monterey, merged in December 1890, and the city incorporated on March 16, 1909.

The Santa Fe railroad arrived that same year, and in 1923 the legislature chose Lubbock for Texas Technological College, renamed Texas Tech University in 1969. A medical school followed in 1970. The Handbook counts seven hospitals with over 2,000 beds, which anchors health care as a major employer.

Farming still shapes the economy. Irrigation pushed the region toward cotton and sorghum in the 1930s, and Lubbock became a wholesale hub for dozens of West Texas and eastern New Mexico counties. Reese Air Force Base closed in 1997, and its land became the Reese Technology Center.

Weather is part of local memory. A tornado struck the city center on May 11, 1970 and killed twenty-six people. Expect inspectors and buyers to look hard at roofs, hail damage and storm protection.

sections.h2: Who bills Lubbock property tax, and what changed in 2026?
sections.html:
The Lubbock Central Appraisal District values property and collects on behalf of local units. Texas levies no state property tax, so your bill is the sum of local rates.

The district reported mailing 2026 statements on October 23, 2026, and said bills for Lubbock Cooper ISD would wait for the result of a November 3, 2026 voter-approval tax rate election. If your house is in that school district, ask the district office which rate your bill uses.

At the state level, the lien for a year's tax attaches January 1 and unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1. In a sale, your title company normally splits the year's bill between you and the buyer, so look for that line on the settlement statement.

One warning on the district's own home page deserves repeating: firms sometimes charge a one-time processing fee to file a homestead exemption, and the district says filing never costs anything.

sections.h2: Which homestead breaks can Lubbock owners claim?
sections.html:
Owners can file for a residence homestead exemption online through the district's property search. The district lists the general exemption and separate ones for disabled owners, seniors, 100 percent disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses.

  • Every Texas school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and seniors or disabled owners get a further $60,000 off the school levy base.
  • Appraised value on a homestead may grow no more than 10 percent a year, counting from the year after the exemption begins.
  • Seniors and disabled owners may defer taxes while they own and live in the house, with the debt, penalty and interest falling due 181 days after the property stops qualifying.

Questions go to 806-762-5000. Because an exemption does not travel with the seller, a buyer who moves in applies for a new one.

sections.h2: How do I pay or look up taxes on a Lubbock house?
sections.html:
Search the account on the district site, mail a check to P.O. Box 10568, Lubbock, TX 79408, drop it at 2109 Avenue Q, or pay online or by phone. Processing charges on card and online payments go to Certified Payments rather than the district.

Online and phone payment charges listed by the Lubbock Central Appraisal District
Payment methodCharge as printed
Electronic checkFlat fee of $1.50
Credit card2.19% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00
Debit card1% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00

If the title company needs a tax certificate, ask the district for one. Accounts that reach tax foreclosure involve a notarized written-statement request, form 50-307, with a $10.00 fee in certified funds.

sections.h2: What if a Lubbock owner is late on the mortgage or taxes?
sections.html:
Options shrink with each missed month, so move early. A lender must give a default notice with twenty days to catch up, and an auction notice must come three weeks ahead. Auctions run monthly, during daytime hours, in an area the county designates.

Back taxes work differently. A collector may offer a payment plan of up to 36 months on a homestead, and penalty relief is possible if you pay quickly and ask in writing.

  • A sale ahead of the auction protects equity and keeps a foreclosure off your record.
  • Ask the lender for a payoff figure, and about a short sale if the balance tops value.
  • Search county records for liens so nothing surprises the title company.

sections.h2: Can Lubbock estates and rented houses sell fast?
sections.html:
Yes, once the paperwork is sorted. For an inherited house, a will may be probated up to four years after death, and a muniment of title can let the will and court order stand in for a full administration. Without a will, a small estate affidavit covers modest estates, while an affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement that a buyer may refuse.

A rented house raises timing questions. Written notice to leave is normally three days, a justice court hears the case, and a writ of possession is available six days after judgment. Cash buyers often accept a tenant in place, which skips that sequence.

sections.h2: Where is a Lubbock deed filed?
sections.html: The Lubbock County Clerk keeps the official records. A notary or similar officer must acknowledge the signature first. Ask the clerk for the fee schedule, since state caps and county charges vary, and expect the closing agent to file and pay from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lubbock house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take houses as they are, so a worn roof or old plumbing does not have to be fixed first. Expect the offer to reflect repair cost, and set it beside an agent's listing price before you choose.

faqs.q: When do Lubbock property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: Texas treats most unpaid taxes as delinquent on February 1, when penalty and interest begin. The Lubbock district publishes statement dates on its site, and its office can confirm your account at 806-762-5000.

faqs.q: Does filing a homestead exemption in Lubbock cost anything?
faqs.a: No. The appraisal district says there is never a charge to file any exemption, and it warns owners to ignore firms asking for a one-time processing fee.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien stop a Lubbock sale?
faqs.a: It complicates the sale but does not stop it. The lien attaches each January 1, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid, which a title company can do from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Who files the deed when a Lubbock house sells?
faqs.a: The title company normally submits it to the Lubbock County Clerk. The signature must be acknowledged before a notary, and the clerk can quote the recording charges.
